correctness.rationale: The independence wording in the Finding is false if applied literally to the normalized residual Z defined in the assumptions. The padded n-vector Z has its unique zero at I almost surely, so P(Z_i=0 | I=i)=1 while P(Z_i=0)=1/n. The proof instead establishes mutual independence of m, I, and the (n−1)-tuple of nonminimum residual coordinates read in original-index order after deleting I. This distinction does not invalidate the majorization or covariance. On the minimum-i chamber, retaining all but one of the other coordinates gives a Jacobian proportional to (1−nt)^(n−2), so the deleted tuple is uniform on its simplex, independent of t and i. The equal chamber masses give uniform I; integrating or taking the volume of {X_j≥t all j} gives P(m≥t)=(1−nt)^(n−1). Thus nm is Beta(1,n−1), with Var(m)=(n−1)/(n^4(n+1)). Padding the independent tuple at the sampled index gives the correct conditional coupling X_t=t1+(1−nt)Z. For s<t<1/n this mixes X_s with the barycenter with weight λ=(1−nt)/(1−ns) on X_s; all top-k sums are pulled toward k/n and X_s≠X_t. This proves simultaneous Schur order (and strict inequality for strictly Schur-convex statistics), using a regular conditional version. The residual maximum of n−1 components has mean H_(n−1)/(n−1), via integrating the inclusion–exclusion survival function. Hence Cov(m,M)=Var(m)[1−n H_(n−1)/(n−1)]=(1−H_n)/(n^3(n+1)). Independently the minimum of n iid exponentials has rate n and is independent of the maximum of the n−1 exponential excesses; E[min·max]=2/n²+H_(n−1)/n, and the gamma total has independent square moment n(n+1), confirming the formula. At n=2 the deleted tuple is the constant 1, M=1−m and the covariance is −1/48. The finite rational checker was inspected rather than executed. If 'residual simplex point' is read as the deleted tuple in the proof, that intended independence statement is correct; it is not independence of the defined Z and I.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Averaging with the barycenter is a doubly stochastic map, so the same common-residual coupling immediately supplies all Schur-convex inequalities, rather than needing any validation for a class of test functions. Taking the maximum before averaging over the residual gives an affine mean, so its covariance with the minimum is its slope times the beta variance. The earlier result is for n≥3, but n=2 is the single automatic identity M=1−m and not a substantive extension.

value.rationale: A simultaneous dependence statement has a natural interpretation, but here the stronger-sounding order is the direct barycentric contraction of a previously given conditional sample. Once this is recognized, the exact extreme covariance is a beta variance multiplied by an affine slope involving a classical first moment. Correctly distinguishing the deleted and padded residuals repairs the wording only; it leaves no independently new and substantive remainder to accept.
